title: You would think that is a basic football concept. It is the most basic. And yet, look how fans and teams talk and behave. Do you think all teams and fans act as though the regular season is the playoffs? They are. Way less games in a NFL regular season than a NBA or MLB playoffs. It is the playoffs. I’ve been to a ton of regular season and playoff games for various teams. The energy is different. So, obviously my obvious point isn’t obvious to all. And then the actual playoffs being single elimination is a brutality that doesn’t care how hurt your team is. And yet, in the summer, all sorts of couch-sitting predictor people have ridiculous expectations for teams, like the Bills, as though this is easy, a short regular season with different schedule strengths and any team able to win, leading to brutal single elimination games. One of the best reality programs in the world.

title: Jalen Hurts Training Camp Stats, Day 5: Tuesday was one of the most choppy, discombobulated practices I’ve ever covered The offense performance was filled with backups and flags. Both Devonta Smith and Makai Lemon missed practice due to hamstring injuries. Lane Johnson was once again an excused absence Add in a decision by the coaching staff to have a few periods with (basically) an entire backup offensive line and there were stretches of practice where Jalen Hurts was on the field with 9 or 10 players that weren’t on the team last season Those factors have to go into account when judging Hurts day. He had two nice completions to Wicks, one of which was on third down vs Quinyon. It does seem like Wicks and Hurts are starting to develop some nice chemistry. Because of all the flags (I counted at least seven) the offense really never got going. The 6/19 has to be one of the lowest days I’ve ever charted, but it wasn’t really Hurts fault. His interception was probably a poor decision though as he threw it deep to Hollywood Brown who was double covered. It was picked off by Michael Carter. The offense did get into the end zone once on a throw from Hurts to Brown from about 5-yards out but it was called back due to an illegal formation. Overall it was a day that could have some benefit as Hurts got lots of reps with lots of backups. On the other hand it is probably a day Hurts won’t want to repeat anytime soon. Day 5 Stats: 6/19, 0 TD, 1 INT 2026 Stats: 60/91, 3 TD, 2 INT Grade: C+

The offense performance was filled with backups and flags. Both Devonta Smith and Makai Lemon missed practice due to hamstring injuries. Lane Johnson was once again an excused absence 

Add in a decision by the coaching staff to have a few periods with (basically) an entire backup offensive line and there were stretches of practice where Jalen Hurts was on the field with 9 or 10 players that weren’t on the team last season

His interception was probably a poor decision though as he threw it deep to Hollywood Brown who was double covered. It was picked off by Michael Carter. 

The offense did get into the end zone once on a throw from Hurts to Brown from about 5-yards out but it was called back due to an illegal formation. 

Overall it was a day that could have some benefit as Hurts got lots of reps with lots of backups. On the other hand it is probably a day Hurts won’t want to repeat anytime soon.

title: “I love the Dolphins and the people here, but after 13 years it was just the right time for me to make this decision,” said Garfinkel in a statement. “The business has never been in a better place and the team of people we have here is second to none in sports. I want to thank the South Florida community and Dolphins fans for all of their support over the years and especially Steve Ross for the opportunity to be a part of this great organization. He is a visionary leader and a team owner who always strives to be best-in-class, and he provides his people all the trust and resources needed to be successful. title: Dennis Allen was asked about expectations for several players who will be stepping into new/unfamiliar roles with injuries at nickel and safety. To sum it up, this was as fired up as I've seen him answer any one question in awhile. Allen: "I just want to…everybody asks, ‘What do you want to see out of this guy? What do you want to see out of this guy? What do you want to see out of this guy?’ You know what I want to see? I want to see 11 frickin’ dudes on the field competing their ass off. And if we all do that, then I feel pretty confident that we’ll get them to the right spot. But that’s what this time of year is all about. This is about developing the culture and the way that you’re going to play. That’s what I want to see out of all of them. I want to see it out of the frickin’ 10 year vet, I want to see it out of the rookie."

I want to see 11 frickin’ dudes on the field competing their ass off. And if we all do that, then I feel pretty confident that we’ll get them to the right spot. But that’s what this time of year is all about. This is about developing the culture and the way that you’re going to play. That’s what I want to see out of all of them. I want to see it out of the frickin’ 10 year vet, I want to see it out of the rookie."

During zone, the defender's to this side -- do I put it a way to maximize run after catch? He has the ability to pinpoint the ball into the right location. He has always had that trait. Now in a new system, can he elevate that further? That's the command I'm looking for from those spots. That's the thing, right now, that's so impressive to me. "There was a deep ball to Terry (McLaurin) that was completed just in the best location that went over Mike (Sainristil) and into that location. That's not luck. That's super hard to do. title: There are almost endless reasons why Bijan Robinson deserves this record breaking deal. No one had forced or created more missed tackles or plays over 10 yards last season. He had more scrimmage yards over the last two years than anyone. Or that he's an offensive weapon, not a RB. But if you ask coaches, it's that he's an eraser. Any mistake within a play from the call to a block can be erased by Bijan and he can still find a way to not only create positive yardage, but an explosive play. That's the rarest of rare and he has it.

title: Dallas Cowboys Training Camp presented by American Airlines is returning to Ford Center at The Star in Frisco on Aug. 25 & 26. The Dallas Cowboys will return from their portion of Training Camp in Oxnard, California, to host two open practices as part of the 2026 Training Camp presented by American Airlines at Ford Center at The Star in Frisco. Training Camp practices provide fans the opportunity to see Dallas Cowboys players and coaches as they prepare for the 2026 season. The Training Camp schedule in Frisco will kick off on Tuesday, August 25 at 5:30 p.m. with an Opening Ceremony presented by American Airlines, including a performance by the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and remarks from Cowboys Owner, President and General Manager Jerry Jones and American Airline Director of Partnerships and Community Relations, Griffin Gonzalez, ahead of the 6:00 p.m. two-hour open practice session. Fans can also enjoy appearances by Cowboys mascot Rowdy and interactive fan activations throughout the evening. For the first time ever, a post-practice tailgate and drone show will take place outside on Tostitos Championship Plaza from 8:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., featuring player appearances, a performance by the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, and a special announcement as part of the evening's programming.

title: QB Drake Maye, to @SiriusXMNFL, with a breakdown of the Patriots’ top WRs: “Start off the bat with A.J. [Brown], having him coming in and kind of set the tone for the room. I think him and Romeo [Doubs] -- the guys in there, they’ve really enjoyed the competitive drive in that room. People say it’s a crowded room but, as you know as receivers go, you’re going to need everybody. “With A.J., the ability for him to not only make me look good, but go out there and make plays and catch the football; we were watching some of his ‘target tape’ the other day, and him being able to take a slant, take an under, and take it to the house. But at the same time he has route craft and he knows you can’t just win everything physically. At some point, you have to use routes, use his technique, and he does a great job. “I think Romeo has done a great job coming in here and learning the offense. He hasn’t been in an offense like this that has some decision-making [for receivers]. I think he’s getting better and better as he’s gotten through OTAs and even in camp, he’s making some great plays for us. He’s kind of shifty and has a little wiggle to him that I didn’t really expect throwing to him in camp. “Next up, we have Pop [Douglas] in the slot. I think Pop’s the one from last year that’s just continuing to get better and better. You see it every year. From my rookie year being with him to Year 3 now, just kind of the connection and knowing how he runs routes. I think he does a great job in man; it’s hard to cover him. So he’s going to be a big piece of what we do when we’re in ‘11’ personnel. I’m looking forward to seeing how he continues to grow and make more plays this year. I think he definitely will. “Mack [Hollins] is kind of the Swiss-Army knife. He does it all. He’s obviously big in the run game, but I think Coach [McDaniels] rewards him with play-action off it. So he always says, ‘Just throw it to me on the in-cuts.’ He loves [that]. He’s big and has that demeanor to him that people feed off, that energy about him. “Kyle [Williams], last year, was kind of a big-play guy. title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 6: - A long session for the Niners coming off a walk through on Sunday. They'll get a full day off tomorrow and begin another practice block on Wednesday. - Coach Kyle Shanahan continues to look like he's making progress in his recovery from injuries suffered in a car crash. Shanahan came out to the field at 10:39 today and was again out there for the rest of the session after. He stood in mid-center field for some of it and moved around a bit from there. He also took part in the breakdown at the end before passing it to another successful head coach... - Mike Brown, the NBA champion Knicks' coach, was in attendance and got to break down the huddle at the end. Brown's son, Cameron, is the team's defensive quality control coach. - Alex Smith, the former Niners QB and current ESPN analyst, was also in the house today. - New additions on the injury front: WR Mike Evans (quad strain) and RB Kaelon Black (adductor). They did not participate. WR De'Zhaun Stribling (hamstring tightness) also did not practice again. Saw Evans and Stribling doing some running and work on the side. Both seem to be moving OK. - Also doing work on the side today: WR Christian Kirk (calf) and DT Gracen Halton (knee bone bruise). Also saw CB Jack Jones doing some work on the side though he was in uniform and doing some regular practice things as well. - The other non participants today: S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), RB Jordan James (rib), DL Keion White (adductor), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle), DL Cam Sample (knee). - DT CJ West and EDGE Romello Height (elbow) were back at practice. - DL Mykel Williams and RB Isaac Guerendo continue to get plenty done on the side as well as they work back from PUP list. - Spotted during individual drills: LB Jaden Dugger doing some work with the defensive line group. The Niners liked Dugger's versatility coming out and seem to want to explore all the ways that can be used, though it doesn't hurt that they're short on bodies at that spot right now because of injuries. - With numbers down on the DL, there were no one-on-one pass rush drills today. The Niners did a lot more mixing and matching all over on Monday in general. - The offense and QB Brock Purdy bounced back a bit today despite all the moving parts at wide receiver. Had him at 14-of-21 though there wasn't a lot going down the field. Purdy just missed TE Jake Tonges on a deep ball late in practice and S Ji'Ayir Brown broke up a would-be TD in the red zone for Tonges on a well thrown ball. A nice play by Brown, though. - Speaking of Brown, he had some interesting things to say after practice. He talked openly about how much fun he's having and how Raheem Morris' scheme allows him to play to his strengths (instincts and reading the QB) more than previous one. He has been around the ball a lot in this camp and got his hands on the ball multiple times. A big season for him going into a contract year. - Both corners -- Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green -- were again sticky in coverage today. Even when completions were made, they were right there and both had a PBU or two. - Receiver and edge rusher aren't the only spots hit by injuries. For a team hoping to get RB Christian McCaffrey more breathers, it's not great that the three guys behind him on the depth chart -- James, Black, Guerendo -- aren't on the field. A lot of work for Patrick Taylor and Sincere McCormick right now. - Height flashed his bend and speed off the edge during team. There's little doubt he has some pass rushing chops. I just don't imagine the Niners want him to be a hand in the ground edge in four-down looks that much so much as sprinkling him in there in obvious passing situations and deploying him as the fifth guy when they go five down. Still plenty of time for that to sort, though. - Junior Bergen was drafted to be a returner and landed on the practice squad last year in part because he struggled as a receiver. It looks like he's made some strides in that regard so far in camp. Not saying he'd be in the WR rotation or anything, just noting apparent improvement which would help his cause if can handle return duties. - LB Nick Martin continues to flash his speed too. It seems like for him it's just a matter of harnessing that speed and making the right reads so he doesn't overrun plays. That was something that plagued Dee Winters at times but Martin seems to be finding a groove on when to step on the gas and when to let it come to him a bit more. - The 49ers are off tomorrow. They'll be back at it on Wednesday with back to back practices then before a walk through on Friday.
summary:
Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 6:

- A long session for the Niners coming off a walk through on Sunday. They'll get a full day off tomorrow and begin another practice block on Wednesday. 

- Coach Kyle Shanahan continues to look like he's making progress in his recovery from injuries suffered in a car crash. Shanahan came out to the field at 10:39 today and was again out there for the rest of the session after. He stood in mid-center field for some of it and moved around a bit from there. He also took part in the breakdown at the end before passing it to another successful head coach...

- Mike Brown, the NBA champion Knicks' coach, was in attendance and got to break down the huddle at the end. Brown's son, Cameron, is the team's defensive quality control coach. 

- Alex Smith, the former Niners QB and current ESPN analyst, was also in the house today. 

- New additions on the injury front: WR Mike Evans (quad strain) and RB Kaelon Black (adductor). They did not participate. WR De'Zhaun Stribling (hamstring tightness) also did not practice again. Saw Evans and Stribling doing some running and work on the side. Both seem to be moving OK. 

- Also doing work on the side today: WR Christian Kirk (calf) and DT Gracen Halton (knee bone bruise). Also saw CB Jack Jones doing some work on the side though he was in uniform and doing some regular practice things as well. 

- The other non participants today: S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), RB Jordan James (rib), DL Keion White (adductor), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle), DL Cam Sample (knee). 

- DT CJ West and EDGE Romello Height (elbow) were back at practice. 

- DL Mykel Williams and RB Isaac Guerendo continue to get plenty done on the side as well as they work back from PUP list. 

- Spotted during individual drills: LB Jaden Dugger doing some work with the defensive line group. The Niners liked Dugger's versatility coming out and seem to want to explore all the ways that can be used, though it doesn't hurt that they're short on bodies at that spot right now because of injuries. 

- With numbers down on the DL, there were no one-on-one pass rush drills today. The Niners did a lot more mixing and matching all over on Monday in general. 

- The offense and QB Brock Purdy bounced back a bit today despite all the moving parts at wide receiver. Had him at 14-of-21 though there wasn't a lot going down the field. Purdy just missed TE Jake Tonges on a deep ball late in practice and S Ji'Ayir Brown broke up a would-be TD in the red zone for Tonges on a well thrown ball. A nice play by Brown, though.

- Speaking of Brown, he had some interesting things to say after practice. He talked openly about how much fun he's having and how Raheem Morris' scheme allows him to play to his strengths (instincts and reading the QB) more than previous one. He has been around the ball a lot in this camp and got his hands on the ball multiple times. A big season for him going into a contract year. 

- Both corners -- Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green -- were again sticky in coverage today. Even when completions were made, they were right there and both had a PBU or two. 

- Receiver and edge rusher aren't the only spots hit by injuries. For a team hoping to get RB Christian McCaffrey more breathers, it's not great that the three guys behind him on the depth chart -- James, Black, Guerendo -- aren't on the field. A lot of work for Patrick Taylor and Sincere McCormick right now. 

- Height flashed his bend and speed off the edge during team. There's little doubt he has some pass rushing chops. I just don't imagine the Niners want him to be a hand in the ground edge in four-down looks that much so much as sprinkling him in there in obvious passing situations and deploying him as the fifth guy when they go five down. Still plenty of time for that to sort, though.

- Junior Bergen was drafted to be a returner and landed on the practice squad last year in part because he struggled as a receiver. It looks like he's made some strides in that regard so far in camp. Not saying he'd be in the WR rotation or anything, just noting apparent improvement which would help his cause if can handle return duties.

- LB Nick Martin continues to flash his speed too. It seems like for him it's just a matter of harnessing that speed and making the right reads so he doesn't overrun plays. That was something that plagued Dee Winters at times but Martin seems to be finding a groove on when to step on the gas and when to let it come to him a bit more. 

- The 49ers are off tomorrow. They'll be back at it on Wednesday with back to back practices then before a walk through on Friday.

title: A few notes from the #broncos first day in pads: - Saw center Luke Wattenberg get banged up. He was pretty frustrated when it happened. Didn't return. - Garett Bolles deserves some love. He didn't give up a sack last year and was an All-Pro. He's been a staple at LT for Denver for a long time. He had a few exceptional reps against one of the best in the game in Nic Bonitto today. - WR Pat Bryant continues to make plays. He can play x or move to the slot. They'll find ways to create a role for him. very Smart WR with real size. - Riley Moss came down with a jump ball throw to Courtland Sutton. Moss has had a solid early start to camp. - CB Jahdae Barron is not playing safety. He's playing CB, nickel and dime. - You can see some of the wrinkles in the offense or call it an evolution in year 3 with Bo Nix. It's fun to watch what Sean Payton and Davis Webb are taking a look at to dress things up presnap.
summary:
A few notes from the #broncos first day in pads:
- Saw center Luke Wattenberg get banged up. He was pretty frustrated when it happened. Didn't return.
- Garett Bolles deserves some love. He didn't give up a sack last year and was an All-Pro. He's been a staple at LT for Denver for a long time. He had a few exceptional reps against one of the best in the game in Nic Bonitto today. 
- WR Pat Bryant continues to make plays. He can play x or move to the slot. They'll find ways to create a role for him. very Smart WR with real size. 
- Riley Moss came down with a jump ball throw to Courtland Sutton. Moss has had a solid early start to camp. 
- CB Jahdae Barron is not playing safety. He's playing CB, nickel and dime. 
- You can see some of the wrinkles in the offense or call it an evolution in year 3 with Bo Nix. It's fun to watch what Sean Payton and Davis Webb are taking a look at to dress things up presnap.
full_text:
A few notes from the #broncos first day in pads:
- Saw center Luke Wattenberg get banged up. He was pretty frustrated when it happened. Didn't return.
- Garett Bolles deserves some love. He didn't give up a sack last year and was an All-Pro. He's been a staple at LT for Denver for a long time. He had a few exceptional reps against one of the best in the game in Nic Bonitto today. 
- WR Pat Bryant continues to make plays. He can play x or move to the slot. They'll find ways to create a role for him. very Smart WR with real size. 
- Riley Moss came down with a jump ball throw to Courtland Sutton. Moss has had a solid early start to camp. 
- CB Jahdae Barron is not playing safety. He's playing CB, nickel and dime. 
- You can see some of the wrinkles in the offense or call it an evolution in year 3 with Bo Nix. It's fun to watch what Sean Payton and Davis Webb are taking a look at to dress things up presnap.

title: 49ers just wrapped up Block 2 of camp with a reminder of how good Brock Purdy is — even without his top 3 WR (Evans/Stribling injuries are NOT serious), Purdy's offense managed some crisp success: 🏈Demarcus Robinson was Purdy's favorite WR, reminiscent of when 49ers beat Philly with a skeleton crew. The deep out was the duo's bread and better 🏈Best play: Excellent one-handed catch from TE Brayden Willis on a corner route from Mac Jones. 🏈Deommodore Lenoir had two more PBUs — including one on a Purdy-Robinson deep out. CB1 been very active this camp and said this morning on KNBR that he's as locked in as ever 🏈6-3 rookie CB Ephesians Prysock notched a nice reaching PBU vs 5-9 Junior Bergen. 🏈Speaking of Bergen, he's making quite a few plays on offense and I wouldn't be quick to discount him in the punt return battle. FWIW, Bergen has made more offensive plays than Jacob Cowing, with whom he may be in a battle for a 53-man spot 🏈49ers did some red-zone work today where safety Ji'Ayir Brown had a nice, athletic PBU in the corner against TE Jake Tonges. Jordan Watkins later caught a TD from Jones in the corner 🏈New RB Khalil Herbert is wearing No. 40. He dished out some real contact on his first run — at 212 but just 5-9, Herbert is not a player defenders enjoy running in to. He'll be in the KR mix alongside Deebo Samuel — "hell yeah, let's go!" was Boyer's reaction to the Deebo signing 🏈LB Nick Martin dropped what should've been an easy INT from Kurtis Rourke, but he was in correct position. Later he made a nice stop on a Kyle Juszczyk catch 🏈Team drills started with a nice CMC run (he's had a handful already). And yes, as I've stated already and will discuss more, rookie Jaden Dugger worked with the thinned-out DE group for the first time. He did notch a would-be sack. A lot to unpack when it comes to his talent and that move as the 49ers navigate the dog days. More soon...

🏈Team drills started with a nice CMC run (he's had a handful already). And yes, as I've stated already and will discuss more, rookie Jaden Dugger worked with the thinned-out DE group for the first time. He did notch a would-be sack.

A lot to unpack when it comes to his talent and that move as the 49ers navigate the dog days. More soon...

title: #Giants camp takeaways - First day in pads and it was a physical one. Really good day for Arvell Reese. Couple run stops, a TFL and his first sack (beat Andrew Thomas). He’s stating to really come on. - Malachi Fields had a gorgeous grab on a go ball on 7-on-7s. Reached out and made the grab while keeping feet in bounds. Ball hung in the air from Jaxson Dart, but he adjusted to it. Cambre also had one where he ripped it away from the defender. - Micah McFadden (Winston) and Jevon Holland (Dart) had INTs. Dart can get a pass — ball slipped out in the rain. He’s the backup, but Jameis really isn’t having a good start to camp. Missing a lot of throws because he’s just not seeing open guys/late/missing passes. He was 8 of 21 today. - Tae Banks dropped an INT. He should have had the McFadden INT, too. He deflected it. Banks has been in good position a few times this summer. Isn’t catching them. - There was a downpour of rain. The Giants practiced through it. Football weather! Came down for about an hour. - There were a TON of penalties. Frustrating day from that regard. I had 13. Most of them false starts/offsides. Just brutal.

title: Eagles Training Camp Player of the Day, Day 4: Elijah Moore Elijah Moore got a ton of 1st-team reps on Monday with Makai Lemon leaving practice early. For the most part Moore made the most of them. Moore had two really nice catches over the middle, including one that was a 30-40ish yard TD down the middle of the field. His other catch came between the hash marks around 15-20 yards over the middle between multiple defenders. The only downside to Moore’s day was what seemed to be a miscommunication between Hurts and Moore that resulted in an interception in 7v7s. Moore entered camp fighting for a roster spot. On Monday he looked like a player the team should keep on their initial 53-man roster.

Eagles Training Camp Player of the Day, Day 4: Elijah Moore

Elijah Moore got a ton of 1st-team reps on Monday with Makai Lemon leaving practice early. For the most part Moore made the most of them. 

Moore had two really nice catches over the middle, including one that was a 30-40ish yard TD down the middle of the field. His other catch came between the hash marks around 15-20 yards over the middle between multiple defenders. 

The only downside to Moore’s day was what seemed to be a miscommunication between Hurts and Moore that resulted in an interception in 7v7s. 

Moore entered camp fighting for a roster spot. On Monday he looked like a player the team should keep on their initial 53-man roster.
full_text:
Eagles Training Camp Player of the Day, Day 4: Elijah Moore

Elijah Moore got a ton of 1st-team reps on Monday with Makai Lemon leaving practice early. For the most part Moore made the most of them. 

Moore had two really nice catches over the middle, including one that was a 30-40ish yard TD down the middle of the field. His other catch came between the hash marks around 15-20 yards over the middle between multiple defenders. 

The only downside to Moore’s day was what seemed to be a miscommunication between Hurts and Moore that resulted in an interception in 7v7s. 

Moore entered camp fighting for a roster spot. On Monday he looked like a player the team should keep on their initial 53-man roster.

title: Better late than never. Observations from Practice 5, today's workout: 🏈 Daniels keeps getting better and better. Looks way more comfortable. Offense has given the defense more of a run each day seemingly. 🏈 Bill has caught the ball really well. They are also asking him to catch the ball a lot. I haven't seen much of White in that regard, but Bill keeps standing out. He makes strong hands catches in the flat time and time again. 🏈 Rasul Douglas looks like he can still play. Had a nice PBU in tight coverage on Jaylin Lane in the end zone today. He's going to help them at CB. His emergence may have had something to do with Witherspoon stepping away. 🏈 Luke McCaffrey had his best practice of the week and maybe his best practice I've seen in a couple years. Not just in terms of volume of catches -- he had several of them -- but also how open he was getting. He beat Mikey Sainristil a couple times, which is a good sign. 🏈 Dyami Brown made some strong hands catches in traffic a couple times today. I was watching practice with Shannon Harris of the DC Defenders for a few minutes and he was impressed with a couple of his snags. That was an issue for Brown early in his career. 🏈 I really liked seeing Daniels coaching up Antonio Williams on the sideline after a series. He went over to the rookie and was going over a route, mimicking the motion of the route with his hands. You love to see that.
summary:
Better late than never. Observations from Practice 5, today's workout:

🏈 Daniels keeps getting better and better. Looks way more comfortable. Offense has given the defense more of a run each day seemingly. 

🏈 Bill has caught the ball really well. They are also asking him to catch the ball a lot. I haven't seen much of White in that regard, but Bill keeps standing out. He makes strong hands catches in the flat time and time again. 

🏈 Rasul Douglas looks like he can still play. Had a nice PBU in tight coverage on Jaylin Lane in the end zone today. He's going to help them at CB. His emergence may have had something to do with Witherspoon stepping away.  

🏈 Luke McCaffrey had his best practice of the week and maybe his best practice I've seen in a couple years. Not just in terms of volume of catches -- he had several of them -- but also how open he was getting. He beat Mikey Sainristil a couple times, which is a good sign. 

🏈 Dyami Brown made some strong hands catches in traffic a couple times today. I was watching practice with Shannon Harris of the DC Defenders for a few minutes and he was impressed with a couple of his snags. That was an issue for Brown early in his career. 

🏈 I really liked seeing Daniels coaching up Antonio Williams on the sideline after a series. He went over to the rookie and was going over a route, mimicking the motion of the route with his hands. You love to see that.
full_text:
Better late than never. Observations from Practice 5, today's workout:

🏈 Daniels keeps getting better and better. Looks way more comfortable. Offense has given the defense more of a run each day seemingly. 

🏈 Bill has caught the ball really well. They are also asking him to catch the ball a lot. I haven't seen much of White in that regard, but Bill keeps standing out. He makes strong hands catches in the flat time and time again. 

🏈 Rasul Douglas looks like he can still play. Had a nice PBU in tight coverage on Jaylin Lane in the end zone today. He's going to help them at CB. His emergence may have had something to do with Witherspoon stepping away.  

🏈 Luke McCaffrey had his best practice of the week and maybe his best practice I've seen in a couple years. Not just in terms of volume of catches -- he had several of them -- but also how open he was getting. He beat Mikey Sainristil a couple times, which is a good sign. 

🏈 Dyami Brown made some strong hands catches in traffic a couple times today. I was watching practice with Shannon Harris of the DC Defenders for a few minutes and he was impressed with a couple of his snags. That was an issue for Brown early in his career. 

🏈 I really liked seeing Daniels coaching up Antonio Williams on the sideline after a series. He went over to the rookie and was going over a route, mimicking the motion of the route with his hands. You love to see that.
